Fixture: 20_modular_palette_bands_24x24_lossless.jxl
24x24 RGB, 6 flat colour bands, mathematically lossless, effort 7 --
H.5.2 clamp probe: the "must NOT clamp upward on row 0" case

Purpose
-------
Minimal counter-example to the literal reading of the H.5.2 self-correcting
predictor clamp, found while chasing the slice-7 divergence of fixtures 05,
09 and 10. See docs/experiments/2026-08-03-h52-clamp-asymmetry.md.

cjxl turns this into a Palette(begin_c 0, num_c 3, nb_colours 6) whose
6x3 meta-channel is decoded with the SelfCorrecting predictor at every
sample and a single MA-tree branch on property 0 (channel index), so the
decoded palette is a *direct* readout of the weighted predictor: no context
choice, no other predictor, nothing else can absorb an error.

The decisive sample is meta-channel (3, 0). There
`true_err_W = +864`, `true_err_N = true_err_NW = 0` and
`W3 = N3 = NE3 = 576`, so the printed clause's symmetric clamp would force
the prediction to exactly 576. The stream requires 400 -- the unclamped
weighted average -- proving the lower half of the clamp does not apply here.
Fixture 08 (16-bit grey) is the mirror case: same all-zero products, opposite
sign of true_err_W, and there the *upper* half of the clamp is required.

The six colours are deliberately non-monotonic in every component
(R = 36i, G = 77i, B = 151i, all mod 256), so the palette's first row swings
up and down and both signs of true_err_W occur within nine samples.

                Synthetic, written by the Python snippet inside
                tools/make-debug-fixtures.sh -- no third-party image was used,
                converted, or consulted. 24x24 8-bit RGB (PPM P6), six
                4-pixel-wide vertical bands, colour i (i in 0..5) being
                  R = (36 * i) mod 256
                  G = (77 * i) mod 256
                  B = (151 * i) mod 256
                i.e. (0,0,0), (36,77,151), (72,154,46), (108,231,197),
                (144,52,92), (180,129,243).

Verification
------------
djxl decodes it to a PPM byte-identical to the source (checked on every run of
tools/make-debug-fixtures.sh).

Modular features engaged
-------------------------
The palette transform is confirmed by JPXL's own header parse
(Palette{begin_c 0, num_c 3, nb_colours 6, nb_deltas 0, d_pred 0}), not
merely inferred: the fixture decodes bit-exactly through that path. cjxl
itself printed only "Modular, lossless"; jxlinfo is not built in this
checkout.

cjxl is used strictly as a BLACK BOX: it emits conformant streams for JPXL to
parse. libjxl's source is never read. If a rebuild at a different libjxl
revision changes these digests, that is the point of recording them -- do not
silently update them; note the revision change.
